Uniform sample of a stream in one pass

Source: R/sketch.R
rmbl_reservoir.Rd

Vitter's Algorithm R: draws k items from a stream, each item equally likely to be retained, in a single pass and using memory proportional to k rather than to the stream's length. Use it to take a fair sample of a capsule member you cannot hold, or whose length you do not know in advance.

Usage

reservoir_indices(n, k, seed = 42L)

reservoir_sample(x, k, seed = 42L)

Arguments

n

Length of the stream, one non-negative number.

k

Sample size, one non-negative number. Values above the stream length give the whole stream; 0 gives an empty result.

seed

Seed for the core's generator, a whole number from 0 to below \(2^{53}\) (default 42).

x

Vector to sample from.

Value

reservoir_indices() a sorted numeric (double) vector of 1-based positions, of length min(k, n); reservoir_sample() the corresponding elements of x, in their original order.

Details

reservoir_indices() returns the retained positions, so the same sample can be applied to a file read line by line. reservoir_sample() applies it to a vector in memory.

The first k items fill the reservoir; item \(i > k\) then replaces a uniformly chosen slot with probability \(k / i\), so after \(n\) items every item is in the sample with probability \(k / n\) (Vitter 1985). The positions are returned sorted.

The stream is sampled with the core's own generator seeded by seed, not R's, so the sample is reproducible and R's random stream is left alone – a capsule whose sample changed between runs would not be reproducible. The generator is C++ std::mt19937_64, whose output sequence the C++ standard fixes, and each draw is Lemire's unbiased multiply-and-reject on its 64-bit outputs (Lemire 2019), so the same seed gives the same sample on every platform and C++ library. Versions up to 0.5.12 drew with std::uniform_int_distribution, whose algorithm differs between C++ libraries, so their samples for a seed differ from these.

Errors: n or k not one non-negative whole number; n above \(2^{53}\); k above \(10^8\); seed not a whole number from 0 to below \(2^{53}\) (NA included).

References

Vitter JS (1985). Random sampling with a reservoir. ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 11(1), 37–57. doi:10.1145/3147.3165

Lemire D (2019). Fast random integer generation in an interval. ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation 29(1), 3. doi:10.1145/3230636

Examples

# A reproducible sample of 5 from 1000.
reservoir_indices(1000, 5, seed = 1)
#> [1]  33  67 304 630 638
reservoir_sample(letters, 4, seed = 2)
#> [1] "m" "r" "s" "z"

# Reproducible on every platform, and independent of R's own RNG.
identical(reservoir_indices(1000, 5, seed = 1),
          reservoir_indices(1000, 5, seed = 1))
#> [1] TRUE

# Asking for more than the stream holds returns the whole stream.
reservoir_indices(3, 10)
#> [1] 1 2 3

# Every item is equally likely: over many seeds the retained positions
# are spread uniformly rather than favouring the start or the end.
hits <- unlist(lapply(1:400, function(s) reservoir_indices(50, 5, s)))
round(mean(hits))          # near the midpoint, 25.5
#> [1] 26

# sample rows of a data frame
df <- data.frame(id = 1:20, v = (1:20)^2)
df[reservoir_indices(nrow(df), 3, seed = 7), ]
#>   id  v
#> 3  3  9
#> 8  8 64
#> 9  9 81

# a negative size is refused
try(reservoir_indices(10, -1))
#> Error : `k` must be a single non-negative whole number
